Since Firefox is known to be the browser of choice for privacy advocates, I'm sure a lot of you are using it. That's not to say there isn't some settings that may need changed to achieve a higher level of privacy. Here's a short list of settings to tweak.

I've made a table of the preferences, and the values to change them to below.

  1. Open a new tab, type in the address bar: about:config and press Enter

  2. Accept the warning if it comes up.

  3. In the Search Bar, you can type the name of the preference you wish to change.

Preference Name Original Value New Value Description
browser.selfsupport.url http://self-repair.mozilla.org Blank Mozilla Heartbeat
privacy.trackingprotection.enabled False true This is Mozilla’s new built in tracking protection.
geo.enabled true false Disables geolocation.
browser.safebrowsing.phishing.enabled true false Disable Google Safe Browsing and phishing protection. Security risk, but privacy improvement.
browser.safebrowsing.malware.enabled true false Disable Google Safe Browsing malware checks. Security risk, but privacy improvement.
dom.event.clipboardevents.enabled true false Disable that websites can get notifications if you copy, paste, or cut something from a web page, and it lets them know which part of the page had been selected.
network.cookie.cookieBehavior 0 1 0 = Accept all cookies by default. 1 = Only accept from the originating site (block third party cookies). 2 = Block all cookies by default
network.cookie.lifetimePolicy 0 2 0 = Accept cookies normally. 1 = Prompt for each cookie. 2 = Accept for current session only. 3 = Accept for N days
browser.cache.offline.enable true false Disables offline cache.
browser.send_pings true false The attribute would be useful for letting websites track visitors’ clicks.
webgl.disabled false true WebGL is a potential security risk. Source
dom.battery.enabled true false Website owners can track the battery status of your device. Source
browser.sessionstore.max_tabs_undo 0 Even with Firefox set to not remember history, your closed tabs are stored temporarily at Menu -> History -> Recently Closed Tabs.

Sources:

  • https://www.privacytools.io/#about_config

  • http://techdows.com/2015/03/how-to-disable-heartbeat-feedback-feature-in-firefox-37.html
